gradeScale: Letter grades S+ (20) down to F- (0) mapped to a 20-point score; overall = weighted tonality (15%), technicalities (15%) and personal preference (70%). Sheet last updated May 27, 2024; quotes come from each linked review's closing section.

entries.name: SUBTONIC STORM
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it S+ overall (score 20.00/20; tonality S+, technicalities S+, preference S+).
entries.quote: I can probably go on and on with the Storm's greatness, but that could take a long time to write up and I'd just end up blabbering on without no end...

entries.name: Empire Ears Odin
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it S- overall (score 18.85/20; tonality S-, technicalities S, preference S).
entries.quote: I unfortunately don't have any other flagship level IEMs besides the ones I own and I already mentioned that they sound just a little less exciting now after my short time with the Odin. I go to pick it up each time, because I want that thrill of going off into a wonderous candy land.

entries.name: Sony IER-Z1R
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it S- overall (score 18.30/20; tonality S, technicalities S, preference S-).
entries.quote: I am very happy I gave this IEM another chance. I finally have come to understand the hype that came with this Sony IEM at its release. It's really a well put together product, except its shell design and fit.

entries.name: ThieAudio Monarch MKII
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it S- overall (score 18.15/20; tonality S, technicalities S-, preference S-).
entries.quote: All that said, I think the Monarch MK2 is a nice improvement to an already stellar set of products that were released about a year and a half ago in the original Monarch and Clairvoyance.

entries.name: Hidition Viento-B (CIEM)
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it S- overall (score 18.00/20; tonality S+, technicalities A, preference S-).
entries.quote: I'm pretty happy with the Viento-B. It's maybe not for everyone, but definitely something to investigate if you're in the market for a unique reference-style IEM.

entries.name: 64 Audio U12t (m15 Apex module)
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A+ overall (score 17.30/20; tonality S-, technicalities S-, preference A+).
entries.quote: The U12t is a really solid all-arounder and worthy of a lot of the praises I’ve read and heard about in the community and from other reviewers.

entries.name: ThieAudio Monarch
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A+ overall (score 17.15/20; tonality S-, technicalities A+, preference A+).
entries.quote: Clairvoyance and the Monarch, are two of my favorite IEMs that I have listened to, and the fact that they are tri-brid IEMs at a relatively low price makes these two sets a industry disrupter and a market statement from Linsoul and

entries.name: Symphonium Titan
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A+ overall (score 17.15/20; tonality S-, technicalities A+, preference A+).
entries.quote: Does that mean I don’t like the Titan? Nope! I love the tuning of the Titan and they really nailed a good basshead level tuning without ruining the overall sound which can be hard to do. The real question is whether or not I recommend the Titan. WHICH I absolutely recommend!

entries.name: Unique Melody MEST MKII
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A+ overall (score 17.00/20; tonality A+, technicalities A+, preference A+).
entries.quote: It's a constant rotation of something different, and the MEST MK2 is even better at this than the original version in my eyes.

entries.name: Unique Melody MEST
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A+ overall (score 17.00/20; tonality A+, technicalities A+, preference A+).
entries.quote: Listening to so many different genres, I feel like the MEST works pretty well as an all-arounder IEM. Just remember that the IEM itself isn’t what I would call neutral, it has got its own flavor with an emphasis in the lower treble region, as well as a bass lift.

entries.name: 64 Audio Nio (m15 Apex module)
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.85/20; tonality A, technicalities A+, preference A+).
entries.quote: I could probably go on and on with different music and how they perform on the Nio, but overall I am left with a lot of smiles listening to this IEM, which I wasn't totally sure I'd like or not.

entries.name: Sony IER-M9
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.70/20; tonality A, technicalities A, preference A+).
entries.quote: I already have the Hidition Viento-B, and its tuned closer to my neutral preference target, and I prefer a little more air, and a little more upper-mid range than what the IER-M9 provides, but in many ways, I could go either set, as a stand-alone multi-BA IEM to use .

entries.name: Vision Ears VE8
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.70/20; tonality A-, technicalities A+, preference A+).
entries.quote: The VE8 is the tried and true multi-BA setup that comes together in a coherent package that is overly warm and missing a bit of sparkle, but can quickly become a guilty pleasure for it's smooth, rich sound that's easy to listen to.

entries.name: Vision Ears PHoNIX
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.70/20; tonality A-, technicalities A+, preference A+).
entries.quote: I love the appearance of both the EXT and PHoNIX, and the technical ability of both is rock-solid as expected. While the EXT is only perhaps average in this aspect compared to tough competition, it has a likeable tonal balance that will appeal to many.

entries.name: ThieAudio Clairvoyance
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.60/20; tonality S, technicalities A+, preference A).
entries.quote: Clairvoyance and the Monarch, are two of my favorite IEMs that I have listened to, and the fact that they are tri-brid IEMs at a relatively low price makes these two sets a industry disrupter and a market statement from Linsoul and

entries.name: Symphonium Audio Helios
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.45/20; tonality A, technicalities S, preference A).
entries.quote: The Symphonium Helios is a really nice entry to the market. I am quite impressed by its technical ability and it has a tonal balance that I think will make it a favorite amongst many, especially those who enjoy electronic and other sub-bass focused music.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Quintet
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.15/20; tonality A+, technicalities A, preference A).
entries.quote: The Quintet is a good sounding IEM. It can be a little lean and bright for some, but for those looking for a balanced and neutral reference IEM at a relatively affordable price, this is a good option compared to other stuff out there.

entries.name: Symphonium Audio Triton
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.15/20; tonality A+, technicalities A, preference A).
entries.quote: The Triton is another solid release from Symphonium. This IEM has a tasteful and enjoyable tuning, that I don't see too many people disliking.

entries.name: Campfire Audio Andromeda 2020
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.15/20; tonality A, technicalities A+, preference A).
entries.quote: I've said a lot of good positive things about the Campfire Andromeda 2020 and that actually would have surprised me coming into this. I was not a big fan of the original version, but did appreciate it for what it was. This model came in and really took me away.

entries.name: Unique Melody MEST mk3
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.15/20; tonality A, technicalities A+, preference A).
entries.quote: My recommendation for the MEST MK3 is to try different tips. This one can sound pretty different with what tips are thrown on them, as I had already discovered, but almost forgot about, with the original MEST MK1 and MK2 units.

entries.name: Vision Ears Erlkonig
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.15/20; tonality A-, technicalities S-, preference A).
entries.quote: When I first heard of the Erlkonig, the first thing I saw was the price tag. It was a bit absurd. It probably still is. And most IEMs that I've tried at these price-tags are usually nothing more than a show piece.

entries.name: Shuoer EJ07M
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.00/20; tonality A+, technicalities A-, preference A).
entries.quote: Okay, so the Shuoer EJ07M did not actually win this shootout against other similarly priced in-ear monitor competition, and actually fell into last place overall in my random categories. BUT -- It is still a good solid product at its price range, and I'd give it a solid recommendation.

entries.name: FAtFreq MAESTRO SE
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A overall (score 16.00/20; tonality A, technicalities A, preference A).
entries.quote: I do find that its bass texture and resolution to be a bit off of the Maestro SE. You definitely get an upgraded resolution and smoothness throughout with the higher end Maestro, but for those on a tighter budget and looking for a good basshead IEM, the Mini may do the trick.

entries.name: DUNU SA6
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A- overall (score 15.85/20; tonality A, technicalities A-, preference A).
entries.quote: The DUNU SA6 is another solid product from this Chinese brand and one of its first entries into multi-BA IEMs. I think they did a great job with this one, from the tuning, to the nice fitting shell geometry, and to the stunning stabilized wood faceplates with each set being unique.

entries.name: 7Hz Timeless
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A- overall (score 15.85/20; tonality A, technicalities A-, preference A).
entries.quote: For just over $200, the Timeless is one of my new reference IEMs for this price range, maybe up to $500, as you start heading into Dunu SA6 territory.

entries.name: Moondrop Dusk
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A- overall (score 15.75/20; tonality S, technicalities A, preference A-).
entries.quote: The Dusk reduces the treble to a much more enjoyable level, while also boosting the low-end which should appeal to many. I think this unit will be very well-enjoyed for both its tuning and its technical capabilities at the asking price.

entries.name: Hidition Viento-R Univ
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A- overall (score 15.70/20; tonality B+, technicalities A, preference A).
entries.quote: Despite buying the universal version, which has some elevated treble response (some may like it and some may not), I find that the Viento is easily one of the most coherent and natural sounding in-ear monitors I have tried out.

entries.name: Moondrop Blessing 2
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A- overall (score 15.30/20; tonality A, technicalities A, preference A-).
entries.quote: The area where I am a little hesitant to recommend is more along the size and fit of the Blessing 2. It has a very large, yet shallow nozzle which can make uncomfortable for some, including myself.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Quartet
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A- overall (score 15.15/20; tonality A, technicalities A-, preference A-).
entries.quote: The Quartet is a different tuning than prior Kiwi Ears sets and it does it heavier dose of bass and less treble than the rest, making this, by far, the darkest set there is.

entries.name: Campfire Audio Andromeda (pre-2020)
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it A- overall (score 15.00/20; tonality B+, technicalities A, preference A-).
entries.quote: To me, I find the Andromeda to be in the same type of category as the Sennheiser HD6X0 series, where it’s steady, done well and rock solid, but it’s not quite what I was looking for at this time, but still - I can totally understand why it is enjoyable because it checks the box on so many levels.

entries.name: Raptgo Hook-X
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B+ overall (score 14.85/20; tonality A, technicalities B, preference A-).
entries.quote: The HOOK-X puts together an interesting package. It cost just a tad more than its competition, but is one of the rare semi-open in-ears on the market. It has an interesting sound signature that originally I disliked, and as I listened more, you can say that it "hooked" me in.

entries.name: Fearless Crinacle Dawn
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B+ overall (score 14.60/20; tonality S, technicalities B, preference B+).
entries.quote: Dawn comes in a beautiful package full of goodies, and a stunning design. The cable is a bit heavy and some may want to look at alternatives.

entries.name: Vision Ears EXT
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B+ overall (score 14.45/20; tonality B+, technicalities A+, preference B+).
entries.quote: I love the appearance of both the EXT and PHoNIX, and the technical ability of both is rock-solid as expected. While the EXT is only perhaps average in this aspect compared to tough competition, it has a likeable tonal balance that will appeal to many.

entries.name: Lime Ears Terra
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B+ overall (score 14.30/20; tonality A, technicalities B+, preference B+).
entries.quote: Lime Ears has done a good job with the Terra. It is tuned to be an all-arounder, and I think they met that task. I used it across my diverse library of music and I did not find it lacking for any song.

entries.name: Moondrop Starfield 2
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B+ overall (score 14.15/20; tonality A, technicalities B, preference B+).
entries.quote: The Starfield 2 is a continuation of Moondrop's line of lower-end dynamic drivers and it is a safe release. I don't quite know if it's worth upgrading if you already own the previous Starfield or Aria, or even the KXXS or Kanas Pro.

entries.name: FATfreq Maestro Mini
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B+ overall (score 14.15/20; tonality A, technicalities B, preference B+).
entries.quote: So, if you are a big bass lover, but also want something that can actually work across genres well, this is a pretty good IEM, and its priced decently well for a possibly niche area where there isn't a lot of stuff that excels in pure bass quality.

entries.name: Vision Ears Elysium
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B+ overall (score 14.15/20; tonality B+, technicalities A-, preference B+).
entries.quote: The Elysium is the attractive technical wonder with three separate driver types and the new EST technology that doesn't come together in the end, however this is the first EST IEM that I found that makes full use of the treble technology and that I do applaud VE for.

entries.name: Meze Alba
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B+ overall (score 14.00/20; tonality A-, technicalities B, preference B+).
entries.quote: The Alba does everything fairly well. It doesn't have a lot of negatives and compared to many items in its price point, it's quite good.

entries.name: SeeAudio x Crinacle Yume Midnight
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B+ overall (score 14.00/20; tonality A+, technicalities C+, preference B+).
entries.quote: With that said, though, the Midnight is one of the best tuned headphones/IEMs under $200, and I can't overstate that. It is tuned very well. It also fits very well, and comes with a nice bundle of accessories including one of my favorite types of cables.

entries.name: Moondrop Kanas Pro
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.85/20; tonality A-, technicalities B-, preference B+).
entries.quote: In general, I found the Moondrop Kanas Pro to be an extremely welcoming IEM at its price range. I think it has a very engaging and enjoyable sound signature that can appeal to many users and genres.

entries.name: 7Hz Eternal
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.85/20; tonality B+, technicalities B, preference B+).
entries.quote: The Eternal may not have the best looking aesthetic for my tastes, but it does make it up with a good solid-performing sound signature, and decent technical performance. It's not the best in-class, but its an above-average performer and I think is a good addition to the market.

entries.name: Samsung Galaxy Buds
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.55/20; tonality A-, technicalities C, preference B+).
entries.quote: So, I’ve rambled on a bit now, but I have to say, after the month and half of having these new partners-in-crime, I am just puzzled and mystified and how great of an overall package these are. They are simple to use, quick to pair, and just work right.

entries.name: ThieAudio Legacy 4 (on-on)
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.30/20; tonality A-, technicalities B, preference B).
entries.quote: The Legacy 4 is yet another solid addition to the Thieaudio lineup that is continuing to grow and most of the ones I've tried are well-tuned and fit solidly within their price points, except perhaps the Voyager 3.

entries.name: Symphonium Meteor
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.30/20; tonality A-, technicalities B, preference B).
entries.quote: The Meteor is a good IEM. It's not great, and it's nowhere near bad. It's solid. I wish it fit me better, as it would be a really nice, lightweight, attractive looking warm, feel-good, cozy sounding in-ear to have around.

entries.name: DUNU EST 112
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.30/20; tonality B+, technicalities B+, preference B).
entries.quote: Do I like the EST 112? Yes, it's pretty good. Is it my favorite? Probably not. But it does treble a bit differently than other products in this price range, and that's a unique characteristic it has. Dunu has 3 solid units now in this price class that can compete with others.

entries.name: HIDIZS MP145
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.15/20; tonality B+, technicalities B, preference B).
entries.quote: Hidizs has done a good job with this uniquely designed MP145 product. The planar driver choice and tuning is very well done for an all-arounder that has a good warm and full sound. The quality of the design and accessories is very good as well and it is priced right.

entries.name: 7th Acoustics Proxima
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.15/20; tonality B+, technicalities B, preference B).
entries.quote: While it may not be for everyone, I do think those looking for a neutral reference IEM at a low budget cost will be happy with listening to this Proxima set.

entries.name: Moondrop KADENZ
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.15/20; tonality B+, technicalities B, preference B).
entries.quote: Generally speaking, I really liked my time with the Kadenz. It is very well-tuned and its newly found technical performance really improves upon the other Moondrop products in this price-range. It seems like a big step forward in this area and makes package a complete one.

entries.name: SeeAudio Yume
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.00/20; tonality A, technicalities C, preference B).
entries.quote: The Yume is a nice IEM. It fits very well in-line with my tonal preferences and really only lacks some additional character in the way of resolution or transient response to make it stand out.

entries.name: Prisma Azul
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.00/20; tonality B+, technicalities B-, preference B).
entries.quote: The Prisma Azul set out to be a nicely tuned monitor and I think it really does a great job here. The tuning is solid, taking the best parts of the Etymotic lineup and smashing them together, while adding a bit more treble to improve this area that can be a little lacking.

entries.name: Moondrop Aria 2
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.00/20; tonality B+, technicalities B-, preference B).
entries.quote: The Moondrop Aria 2 is a step up from the original Aria, which for a long time, was my baseline, under $100 recommendation.

entries.name: ThieAudio Elixir
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.00/20; tonality B, technicalities B, preference B).
entries.quote: The Elixir is a great value and for a price just slightly above the popular Moondrop single-dynamic drivers, I see this as a step up in resolution and technical performance, while also having a clearly good tonal balance that is perhaps a little more referencey than the Moondrop KXXS, Kanas, Kato,

entries.name: Simgot EM6L
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.00/20; tonality B, technicalities B, preference B).
entries.quote: The EM6L is a solid addition for Simgot with a nice tuning that does lean a tad bright at times. It has good technical ability for price point and comes with a good cable, is comfortable and lightweight, and really does a good job for what you are paying for.

entries.name: Simgot EA500LM
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.00/20; tonality B, technicalities B, preference B).
entries.quote: The EA500LM is another nice addition to the Simgot lineup. It can be sometimes a little lean and bright, but in general, it works well for most genres.

entries.name: Shanling Sono
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.00/20; tonality B, technicalities B, preference B).
entries.quote: The Shanling Sono is a decent IEM and not a bad deal for $79 USD. It is a bass cannon of an IEM and handles it mostly well for the tracks that call out for it.

entries.name: DUNU Vulkan
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.00/20; tonality B, technicalities B, preference B).
entries.quote: Dunu's Vulkan is a nicely tuned set that I think will work well with many genres. It does not actually excel in any one category, but isn't bad in anything either.

entries.name: Dunu Luna
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.00/20; tonality B-, technicalities B+, preference B).
entries.quote: I did not know what to really expect when I got the Luna in.

entries.name: Empire Ears Valkyrie
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B overall (score 13.00/20; tonality C, technicalities A, preference B).
entries.quote: I really didn't go into a very thoughtful and concise description of my sound impressions on this review as I typically do, but that's because my experience with the Valkyrie is just that way, not typical.

entries.name: Tin P1 Max
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.85/20; tonality B, technicalities B-, preference B).
entries.quote: To be completely honest, I think I would have been a lot more impressed with the Tin HiFi P1 Max if it came out before the 7Hz Timeless. But with the Timeless as a measuring stick, its hard to not be a little blasé with the P1 Max. Looking at it more objectively, the P1 Max is worth a buy.

entries.name: Etymotic ER4S
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.85/20; tonality B, technicalities B-, preference B).
entries.quote: The Etymotic ER4SR is a legendary reference class IEM that anyone serious about portable audio should make an effort to try. You might just end up owning a set permanently. It's hard to convey in words how the ER4SRs sound like beyond it's DF nature.

entries.name: Sony MDR-EX1000
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.85/20; tonality B-, technicalities B, preference B).
entries.quote: The Sony MDR-EX1000 represents a dying breed: great single dynamic driver IEMs. Admittedly, it has major flaws in both its tuning and practicality. While its tuning flaws may be fixed with EQ, nothing will change the fact that it has next to no isolation and the somewhat awkward fit.

entries.name: BGVP DM7
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.70/20; tonality B, technicalities C+, preference B).
entries.quote: The BGVP DM7 is my favorite BGVP product to date. They do have a quite a few more coming out in the near future and it’ll be interesting to see how the BGVP DMS sounds like.

entries.name: Ovidius RX-100
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.70/20; tonality B-, technicalities B-, preference B).
entries.quote: The Qin Armor name is perhaps a proper name for this IEM. The styling of the design does have a bit of a chest chain armor look to it, and the overall sound is shielded from going to extreme and for the most part is a rather safe tuning.

entries.name: DUNU Falcon Pro (Reference filter)
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.70/20; tonality B-, technicalities B-, preference B).
entries.quote: The Falcon Pro is a nice entry for Dunu. While I don't think it's something that is uniquely great or a world beater, I do think its a nice overall package when you consider the cable, accessories, and build quality.

entries.name: CustomArt Fibae 7
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.45/20; tonality B+, technicalities B, preference B-).
entries.quote: At the end of the day, I find the CustomArt Fibae 7 a very appealing package despite a generally safe tuning approach.

entries.name: Tin HiFi T4
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.30/20; tonality B+, technicalities B-, preference B-).
entries.quote: I find the Tin Hifi T4 a competent and good IEM, and I’m actually very happy with adding it to my collection. It’s the right type of sound signature for what I enjoy and I’m happy to recommend it at the introductory price, and even a strong consideration at the regular retail price.

entries.name: Mangird Tea
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.15/20; tonality B, technicalities B-, preference B-).
entries.quote: The Mangird Tea is a nice IEM, I think. It's very pleasantly sounding, with a rich, thick tonality, and a lush flavor. I think it's biggest flaw is that it's a tad too intimate, but I never found it to be a deal breaker.

entries.name: Etymotic ER2SE
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.15/20; tonality B, technicalities B-, preference B-).
entries.quote: At the end of the day, this review has kind of gone a little bit all over the place, and maybe I can blame that for writing bits and pieces of it over a week’s time instead of coherently writing it in a shorter period of one or two sittings.

entries.name: Unique Melody Mini MEST
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.15/20; tonality B-, technicalities B, preference B-).
entries.quote: The Mini MEST is a solid addition to the Unique Melody family, which in my limited experience with them has been a hit or miss lineup.

entries.name: SHOZY P20
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.15/20; tonality C+, technicalities B+, preference B-).
entries.quote: This was a quick review and impressions of the P20 from Shozy. It's not bad. It's not good. It's just an okay IEM, and one that is probably very niche in its target audience.

entries.name: ThieAudio Legacy 5
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.00/20; tonality B, technicalities C+, preference B-).
entries.quote: Despite some of the negatives I mentioned in this review, the Thieaudio Legacy 5 is a nice addition to their lineup, and sits confidently between the Legacy 3 and the tribrids, Monarch and Clairvoyance.

entries.name: Kefine Delci
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.00/20; tonality B, technicalities C+, preference B-).
entries.quote: The Delci is a great single DD IEM from Kefine. It's tuned very well to my preferences, and works well with all the genres I threw at it. I am pretty impressed with the sound for the low price of just $59, and this easily becomes one of my recommendations at this price point.

entries.name: AUNE Jasper
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.00/20; tonality B, technicalities C+, preference B-).
entries.quote: The Aune Jasper is a really solid entry into the market for the amp/dac manufacturer. This unit puts a nice package together with a safe, but elegant tuning, decent to good resolution, and a comparable accessory set with a very easy to wear and comfortable shell design.

entries.name: Audio Technica LS200is
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.00/20; tonality B, technicalities C+, preference B-).
entries.quote: I found the Audio Technica LS200iS to be a very good sounding in-ear monitor product that had a good natural clean sound, but also missing a little bit of exciting factor. That doesn’t mean, it’s not enjoyable to listen to though, as it still is, and produces good clean music.

entries.name: TruthEar Gate
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.00/20; tonality B, technicalities C+, preference B-).
entries.quote: The TruthEar Gate seems like a wonderful culmination of this, but I continue to be surprised and impressed with the next best thing and the next market-setter. The budget area is getting quite crowded with a lot of impressive and cheap products now, so it is hard to set yourself apart.

entries.name: DUNU Titan S2
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.00/20; tonality B, technicalities C+, preference B-).
entries.quote: The Titan S2 is a neutral and lean sounding product and one I probably would have enjoyed more a few years back, before I became a bass-enjoying musichead . DUNU includes a great accessory package and their new cable is wonderful to use.

entries.name: Meze Rai Penta
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.00/20; tonality B-, technicalities B-, preference B-).
entries.quote: The Rai Penta’s build is fantastic and the star of the show here. You really do get a great design that is also comfortable to wear for long periods of time, and the accessories package is on par if not topping many other IEMs in this price range.

entries.name: BGVP Art Magic V12
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.00/20; tonality B-, technicalities B-, preference B-).
entries.quote: And that is how it goes for the Art Magic V12. Is it worth the money? That’s a bit up to each individual to decide. I think it can trade blows with the IEMs comparable to it within its price-range, but it doesn’t come to the likes of the qdc Anole VX in multi-BA quality, Sony IER-Z1R or the likes.

entries.name: Moondrop May
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it B- overall (score 12.00/20; tonality B-, technicalities B-, preference B-).
entries.quote: The May is very enjoyable in its typical configuration. It is what I'd expect from a Moondrop product -- consistent, above average to great, and expectedly enjoyable. Like other Moondrop products, this works well for all genres, and comes with everything to get you going.

entries.name: Tin T2 Plus
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C+ overall (score 11.85/20; tonality B, technicalities C, preference B-).
entries.quote: I find the Tin T2 Plus is a nice addition to the Tin Hifi lineup. It adds a warmer flavor to their existing roster, however it still maintains the brighter-than-neutral sound signature that has made their lineup popular.

entries.name: Sony WF-1000XM3
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C+ overall (score 11.85/20; tonality B-, technicalities C+, preference B-).
entries.quote: That said, the WF-1000XM3 is a nice IEM that sounds great for this price range, and one I can recommend, as long as you can deal with the fit.

entries.name: Sony XBA-N3
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C+ overall (score 11.85/20; tonality C+, technicalities B-, preference B-).
entries.quote: In 2016, this was a decent to good IEM at its price point. In 2023, at $300, this is a tough sell. Sony's quality accessories and name isn't enough for it to match the sound quality of the Moondrops, the Dunus, and even things from Samsung and Sennheiser these days.

entries.name: Campfire Solaris 2020
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C+ overall (score 11.60/20; tonality C+, technicalities A-, preference C+).
entries.quote: The Campfire Solaris 2020 edition came with a lot of excitement and anticipation in my view. I really enjoyed the original gold-colored set, but found the shell and design to not match my ear anatomy in any way feasible. When the announcement of a smaller version of it came out, I was thrilled.

entries.name: Dunu DK2001
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C+ overall (score 11.55/20; tonality C, technicalities C+, preference B-).
entries.quote: While I don’t find the DK2001 as fatiguing as other IEMs, I could see that the V-shaped nature could be to some. The DK2001 is the sibling with a more vibrant outfit and stylish looks, and the sound follows suit, with some mor rough edges along the way.

entries.name: Tin HiFi T3
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C+ overall (score 11.15/20; tonality B, technicalities C, preference C+).
entries.quote: The Tin T3 is an actual improvement over the previous T2 and T2 Pro and is probably the most balanced of the three.

entries.name: ThieAudio Legacy 2
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C+ overall (score 11.15/20; tonality B, technicalities C, preference C+).
entries.quote: The Legacy 2 is a really solid new product for the under $100 price point. I think it fits well in this area and its main competitor will be the single dynamic-driver, Moondrop Aria, which presents a similar sound, but at a slightly lower price.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Cadenza
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C+ overall (score 11.15/20; tonality B, technicalities C, preference C+).
entries.quote: The Cadenza is another solid release from Kiwi Ears and is priced just right at only $35 USD. There's been a plethora of budget in-ears released with a 10mm "Be-coated" dynamic driver in the past few months.

entries.name: Shozy Form 1.4
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C+ overall (score 11.15/20; tonality B-, technicalities C+, preference C+).
entries.quote: At the end of the day, I think the tuning of the Form 1.4 is an improvement over the Form 1.1 It fixes the issues I had with treble gain, and strained, and sibilant sound, however I am not totally sure the small fix, which can be patched with EQ, is worth a 2.5X price gap.

entries.name: BGVP DM6
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C+ overall (score 11.15/20; tonality B-, technicalities C+, preference C+).
entries.quote: The DM6 is the fun one of the group. I don’t believe this deserves as much hype as it has gotten, but it is a step up from the DMG and the Whizzer Kylin which are a tier below in cost with a V-Shaped sound signature.

entries.name: Tin T3 Plus
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C+ overall (score 11.00/20; tonality B, technicalities C-, preference C+).
entries.quote: The CRN is a good solid addition to the under $50 market and easily can be put in the top or near top of the bracket in terms of tuning and overall enjoyment.

entries.name: SIVGA QUE
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C+ overall (score 11.00/20; tonality C+, technicalities C+, preference C+).
entries.quote: The Sivga Que is a beautifully designed IEM with a comfortable fit and a nice cable. I really like the simple and modernistic wood look and accessories. The tuning is warm and slight dark, and would appeal to those who really enjoy a smoother and fluid sound, as opposed to a neutral and dynamic one.

entries.name: 7Hz Legato
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C overall (score 10.85/20; tonality C+, technicalities C, preference C+).
entries.quote: The Legato, for all its bass, isn't a bad IEM. Where products with this much bass can be totally ruined by an overly obnoxious treble response. The Legato, instead, has a nicely tuned upper-mid range and treble that is smooth and appealing.

entries.name: Tin T5S
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C overall (score 10.85/20; tonality C, technicalities C+, preference C+).
entries.quote: If you are big fan of Tin Hifi's sound through the past 8 or 9 years, you'll probably enjoy the Tin T5S as it is very much aligned with their house sound, although this time with better bass quantity and extension, and an overall better product design, cable and carrying case.

entries.name: Oriolus Monachaa
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C overall (score 10.75/20; tonality C-, technicalities A, preference C).
entries.quote: I find the Monachaa a bit too treble focused, and that causes much of my music I enjoy to lack body as I feel this product focuses more on the bass and treble than the mid-range.

entries.name: FiR VxV (Five x Five)
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C overall (score 10.70/20; tonality D+, technicalities B-, preference C+).
entries.quote: The FiR VxV isn't exactly my preferential target, nor is one I'd probably consider buying personally, but it is something that I did end up getting a little more familiar with and started to see some of its nuances and little things that I can see someone enjoying.

entries.name: Shozy Form 1.1
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C overall (score 10.45/20; tonality B-, technicalities C+, preference C).
entries.quote: The Form 1.1’s new driver does it’s job and gives the bass and lower midrange a fast, punchy, and very good definition, that is unmatched in the

entries.name: MMR Homunculus
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C overall (score 10.45/20; tonality C, technicalities B, preference C).
entries.quote: In just general tonal performance, I think I prefer the Homunculus over the Thummim, mostly because I prefer a more neutral-ish sound signature and the bass-centric signature of the Thummim can be a bit overwhelming for me.

entries.name: Moondrop Golden Ages TWS
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C overall (score 10.30/20; tonality B, technicalities C-, preference C).
entries.quote: Unfortunately, I don't have the Space Travel or Kato TWS from Moondrop to compare to, but these do compare fairly well to my own collection.

entries.name: MMR Thummim
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C overall (score 10.30/20; tonality C-, technicalities B, preference C).
entries.quote: In just general tonal performance, I think I prefer the Homunculus over the Thummim, mostly because I prefer a more neutral-ish sound signature and the bass-centric signature of the Thummim can be a bit overwhelming for me.

entries.name: TFZ No.3
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C overall (score 10.15/20; tonality C+, technicalities C, preference C).
entries.quote: In the end, I find the TFZ No. 3 to be a good buy at $109 and can stack up against IEMs above it’s price range. For a V-shaped IEM, I’d take it over the

entries.name: KZ ZEX Pro / CRN
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C- overall (score 9.15/20; tonality B-, technicalities D, preference C-).
entries.quote: The CRN is a good solid addition to the under $50 market and easily can be put in the top or near top of the bracket in terms of tuning and overall enjoyment.

entries.name: TenHz T5
entries.verdict: Antdroid grades it C- overall (score 9.15/20; tonality C, technicalities C-, preference C-).
entries.quote: The Tenhz T5 is definitely on the warmer side, and it’s roll-off on treble even more defines its target. While it seems to be lacking detail and sparkle, it does provide a very comfortable listening experience that can easily be used for hours and hours at a time.
